Correct — with the candidate pool unlogged, treatment-only exposures cannot be recomputed on the control side, so nothing is attributable.
Incorrect — latency regressions trip p99 alerts right away, which makes it an explicit failure rather than a silent one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录全部候选和特征，使任一模型都能在同一批候选上事后重算排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replayability means logging all candidates and features so any model can be re-scored on the same candidate set afterwards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序之前从全量物料里召回一个小候选集的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the stage that retrieves a small candidate set from the full catalog before ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级别目标：对延迟或可用性设定的可量化承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO is a service level objective, a measurable target for latency or availability.

scenario: 新闻搜索里突发事件的报道要在几分钟内可被搜到，团队要给新鲜度定一组可监控的指标。
scenario_en: In news search, breaking coverage must be findable within minutes, and the team needs a monitorable set of freshness metrics.
q: 新鲜度评估该盯哪几类指标？（多选）
q_en: Which metric families should freshness evaluation track? (Select all that apply.)
why: 新鲜度可能坏在结果过期、抓取太慢、索引没更新三个不同环节，各要一个指标才能定位；只报总体相关性会把三者混成一次模糊的下降。
why_en: Freshness can break at three different places — stale relevance, slow crawling, or a lagging index — so each needs its own metric to localize the problem.
options: temporal relevance：不同类型 query 的结果多快变过期
crawl latency：内容产生到被抓取之间的延迟
index freshness：索引相对线上最新内容的滞后
训练时用的 GPU 显存占用峰值
options_en: Temporal relevance: how fast results go stale for each query type.
Crawl latency: the delay from content creation to it being crawled.
Index freshness: how far the index lags behind the latest live content.
Peak GPU memory used during training.
optionExplanations: 对；它告诉你哪些 query 需要按时间衰减相关性，哪些常青内容不用。
对；它把“搜不到新闻”定位到抓取环节，而不是排序模型的锅。
对；它暴露抓到了但还没进索引的滞后，也就是发了却搜不到的那段。
错；显存是训练资源指标，和用户能不能搜到刚发布的内容无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it tells you which queries need time decay on relevance and which evergreen ones do not.
Correct — it localizes a missing-news complaint to the crawler rather than the ranking model.
Correct — it exposes content that was crawled but not yet indexed, the classic published-but-unsearchable gap.
Incorrect — GPU memory is a training resource metric, unrelated to whether users can find newly published content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量某类查询的结果多快就变得过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal relevance measures how quickly results go stale for a given query type.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容被创建到被爬虫抓到之间的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Crawl latency is the time from content creation to the crawler fetching it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引内容相对线上最新内容的滞后程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index freshness measures how far the search index lags behind the latest live content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器：训练深度模型的主要算力硬件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU is the graphics processing unit hardware that does most deep model training.

scenario: 聊天助手上线一年后，BLEU 和自动事实检查通过率都稳定在 0.97 附近，两个候选模型分不出高下，但用户投诉仍在增加。
scenario_en: A year after launch, the chat assistant's BLEU and automated fact-check pass rate both sit near 0.97, two candidate models look identical, yet user complaints keep rising.
q: 这种指标停滞说明什么该改？
q_en: What does this metric stagnation tell you needs to change?
why: 指标会饱和：系统成熟后旧指标顶到天花板就失去区分度，必须换更难的测试集或更细的维度；代价是新旧版本的历史分数不再直接可比。
why_en: Metrics saturate — once a mature system tops out an old metric it stops discriminating, so evaluation itself must evolve, at the cost of breaking comparability with historical numbers.
options: 说明模型已经足够好了，可以停掉评估投入把资源全部转去做新功能开发
说明指标已经饱和，评估体系本身要随系统成熟而演进
说明测试集样本量不够，只要把同样分布的样本再扩大十倍就能重新分出差距
说明应该改用更宽松的通过阈值，这样两个模型之间的分数差异会被放大出来
options_en: It means the model is good enough, so evaluation spend can move to building new features.
It means the metrics have saturated and the evaluation suite must evolve as the system matures.
It means the test set is too small, and ten times more samples from the same distribution would separate them.
It means you should loosen the pass threshold so the gap between the two models gets amplified.
optionExplanations: 错；投诉还在涨说明失败模式真实存在，只是现有指标看不到它。
对；换更难的分层测试集或拆出新维度，才能重新获得区分度。
错；同分布样本再多也只是把同一个天花板测得更精确，差距依旧为零。
错；调阈值只是移动刻度，不会引入任何关于失败模式的新信息。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — complaints are still rising, so real failure modes exist; the current metrics just cannot see them.
Correct — a harder stratified test set or new sub-dimensions are what restore discriminating power.
Incorrect — more samples from the same distribution only measure the same ceiling more precisely; the gap stays zero.
Incorrect — moving the threshold just rescales the same numbers without adding information about failure modes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双语评估替补：按 n-gram 重合度衡量生成文本与参考答案的相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU scores generated text by n-gram overlap against reference answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标接近上限后不同模型的分数几乎一样，失去区分能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Saturation is when a metric nears its ceiling and stops separating different models.

scenario: 营销文案生成的人工评分只有一个 1-5 的好不好总分，两个评审经常给同一段文案打 2 分和 4 分，且说不清分歧在哪。
scenario_en: Human review of marketing copy uses a single 1-5 overall quality score; two reviewers often give the same text a 2 and a 4 and cannot say where they disagree.
q: 怎么让这个主观评分变得可测？
q_en: How do you make that subjective score measurable?
why: 把好不好拆成 fluency、coherence、style 等各自可判定的子维度，分歧才能定位到具体维度并写进标注规范；代价是每条样本的标注成本翻几倍。
why_en: Break overall quality into separately judgeable aspects like fluency, coherence, and style so disagreement localizes to one dimension, at the cost of several times more annotation work per sample.
tradeoff: 单一总分（便宜但评审一致性差）vs 拆分子维度（一致性高但标注成本翻几倍）
options: 把评审人数从 2 人加到 7 人，取中位数当最终分，用人数把噪声平均掉
拆成 fluency、coherence、style 等子维度分别打分
改用 BLEU 之类的自动重合度分数彻底取代人工评审，直接绕开一致性问题
只保留总分但把量表从 1-5 换成 1-100，让评审有更细的刻度可以选择
options_en: Raise the panel from two to seven reviewers and take the median so noise averages out.
Split the score into aspects such as fluency, coherence, and style.
Replace human review entirely with an automated overlap score like BLEU to sidestep agreement issues.
Keep one overall score but switch the scale from 1-5 to 1-100 for finer granularity.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要在两个候选之间排序而不需要诊断，成对偏好比较比拆维度更快也更一致。
optionExplanations: 错；人多只是摊薄噪声，评审心里的标准仍然不同，分歧原因照样查不出。
对；分歧落到具体维度后可以写进标注规范，也能定位模型弱在哪一项。
错；营销文案没有唯一参考答案，重合度分数对风格和语气几乎没有信号。
错；刻度更细只会让主观分更分散，没有解决在评什么这个根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — more reviewers only dilutes noise; their internal standards still differ and the cause of disagreement stays hidden.
Correct — once disagreement lands on a named aspect it can be written into the labeling guide and traced to a model weakness.
Incorrect — marketing copy has no single reference answer, so overlap scores carry almost no signal about tone or style.
Incorrect — a finer scale just spreads subjective scores further without fixing what is actually being judged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成文本的语法和用词是否自然通顺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fluency is whether the generated text reads naturally and grammatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整段内容前后逻辑是否一致、不自相矛盾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coherence is whether the passage stays logically consistent from start to end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让评审在固定档位（如 1-5）上给出主观程度评分的量表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Likert scale asks raters to score on a fixed set of levels such as one to five.

scenario: 面向青少年的助手，放出一条违法内容会引来监管处罚和品牌事故；误拦一条安全回答只会让用户重问一次。
scenario_en: For a teen-facing assistant, letting one illicit response through means regulatory penalties and brand damage, while wrongly blocking a safe answer just makes the user retry.
q: 安全评估的主指标该盯哪个？
q_en: Which metric should safety evaluation track as its primary number?
why: 漏放一条危险输出的代价远高于误伤一条安全输出，所以安全评估以 false-negative rate 为主指标；代价是拦截更激进，正常回答的误拦率随之上升。
why_en: Missing one harmful output costs far more than wrongly flagging a safe one, so safety evaluation leads with false-negative rate and accepts a higher false-positive rate as the price.
tradeoff: 压低 false-negative（少漏危险但误拦多）vs 压低 false-positive（体验顺但漏放风险高）
options: false-negative rate：危险输出被安全过滤器放过去的比例
整体 accuracy：安全分类器在全部样本上判断正确的比例有多高
prompt-response latency：用户发出请求到看到回答之间等待了多久
false-positive rate：安全输出被误拦下来、让用户不得不重问一次的比例
options_en: False-negative rate: the share of harmful outputs the safety filter lets through.
Overall accuracy: how often the safety classifier is correct across all samples.
Prompt-response latency: how long the user waits between asking and seeing an answer.
False-positive rate: the share of safe outputs wrongly blocked, forcing the user to ask again.
whenOtherWins: 如果场景是低风险的内部工具、误拦会直接卡住工作流，就该反过来先压 false-positive。
optionExplanations: 对；它直接对应危险内容流到青少年用户面前这个不可接受的后果。
错；危险样本占比极低，accuracy 会被大量安全样本主导而看起来很漂亮。
错；延迟是体验指标，和内容安不安全是两个正交的维度。
错；误拦只让用户重问一次，代价远低于放过一条违法内容。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it maps directly onto the unacceptable outcome of harmful content reaching teen users.
Incorrect — harmful samples are rare, so accuracy is dominated by safe ones and looks great regardless.
Incorrect — latency is an experience metric, orthogonal to whether the content is safe.
Incorrect — a wrongly blocked answer just costs one retry, far less than letting illicit content through.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实为危险内容却被模型判为安全的情况。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative is harmful content that the model wrongly judges to be safe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本来安全的内容被模型判为危险而拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is safe content that the model wrongly flags as harmful.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全部预测中判断正确的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Accuracy is the fraction of all predictions that are correct.

scenario: 助手的安全测试集是半年前写好的固定 prompt 集合，通过率一直 99.8%，但社区论坛上不断出现新的绕过写法。
scenario_en: The assistant's safety test set is a fixed prompt list written six months ago with a steady 99.8 percent pass rate, yet community forums keep posting new jailbreak phrasings.
q: 这套安全评估还缺哪一环？
q_en: What is missing from this safety evaluation?
why: 固定测试集只覆盖已知攻击面，新绕过写法天然不在集合里；要靠定期红队主动构造对抗输入找漏洞，代价是需要持续投入专门人力且结果不可复现。
why_en: A frozen test set only covers known attacks, so new jailbreaks are absent by construction; regular red-teaming actively hunts vulnerabilities, at the cost of ongoing specialist effort.
tradeoff: 固定回归集（可重复可比较但只盖已知攻击）vs 定期红队（能发现新漏洞但结果不可复现）
options: 定期红队与对抗性评估，主动构造新攻击找漏洞
把这个安全测试集的规模从一千条 prompt 扩大到一万条同类改写的 prompt
提高安全分类器的拦截阈值，把所有稍微沾边的敏感回答一律直接拒绝掉
把安全评估的运行频率从每周一次提高到每天一次，让同一套用例跑得更勤
options_en: Regular red-teaming and adversarial evaluation that actively construct new attacks.
Grow the safety test set from a thousand prompts to ten thousand rephrasings of the same ones.
Raise the safety classifier threshold and refuse anything remotely sensitive outright.
Run the same suite daily instead of weekly so the existing cases execute more often.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型和策略都冻结、只做上线前回归验证，固定测试集的可重复性反而更有用。
optionExplanations: 对；只有主动对抗才能覆盖还没出现在测试集里的新绕过方式。
错；同类改写扩十倍，覆盖的仍是同一批已知攻击面，通过率照样虚高。
错；一刀切拒绝会大量误伤正常问题，也测不出真正的漏洞在哪。
错；同一套用例跑得再勤，漏掉的攻击方式依然一次都不会被执行到。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — only adversarial probing reaches jailbreaks that are not yet in the test set at all.
Incorrect — ten times more rephrasings still cover the same known attack surface, keeping the pass rate falsely high.
Incorrect — blanket refusal harms many legitimate questions and still reveals nothing about real vulnerabilities.
Incorrect — running the same cases more often never executes the attack patterns they omit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门扮演攻击者、主动构造对抗输入去找系统漏洞的团队或流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A red team deliberately plays attacker, crafting adversarial inputs to find system vulnerabilities.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用特殊措辞诱导模型绕过安全策略输出被禁内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A jailbreak is a phrasing that tricks the model into bypassing its safety policy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入给生成模型的那段指令或问题文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prompt is the instruction or question text given to a generative model.

scenario: 客服机器人的测试集是从三年历史工单里随机抽的；新产品线上线后线上失败率翻倍，测试集通过率却纹丝不动。
scenario_en: A support bot's test set is randomly sampled from three years of tickets; after a new product line launches, live failure rate doubles while test-set pass rate does not move.
q: 测试集该怎么重建才能跟上分布漂移？
q_en: How should the test set be rebuilt to keep up with distribution shift?
why: 随机抽样把新旧工单混在一起，新产线只占极小比例；改成按时间 hold-out 并维护近期流量的滚动窗口，测试集才跟着用户漂移，代价是跨版本分数不再直接可比。
why_en: Random sampling drowns the new product line in three years of old tickets; hold out by time and keep a rolling window of recent traffic so the test set drifts with users.
tradeoff: 随机划分（分数稳定可比但滞后于真实流量）vs 时间 hold-out 加滚动窗口（跟得上漂移但历史分数不可比）
options: 按时间 hold-out，并维护一个近期流量的滚动窗口
把三年工单按产品线分层抽样，保证每条老产品线在测试集里的占比完全相同
把测试集扩大到十万条随机工单，用绝对样本量保证新产品线也能被抽到几条
固定不动这个测试集当长期基准，新产品线的问题交给线上监控去发现
options_en: Hold out by time and maintain a rolling window of recent traffic.
Stratify the three years of tickets by product line so every legacy line keeps an identical share.
Grow the set to a hundred thousand random tickets so sheer volume catches a few new-line cases.
Freeze the set as a long-term benchmark and let production monitoring catch new-product issues.
whenOtherWins: 作为漂移探针的 golden canary 集必须固定不动，那套集合就该冻结而不是滚动。
optionExplanations: 对；时间切分保证测试数据永远晚于训练数据，滚动窗口让它跟上当前流量。
错；按老产品线配平只会锁死旧分布，新产品线仍然拿不到任何配额。
错；十万条里新产线占比依旧很低，几条样本无法把失败率抬进指标。
错；等线上监控报警时用户已经受损，评估失去了上线前拦截的作用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a time split guarantees test data postdates training data, and the rolling window keeps it aligned with current traffic.
Incorrect — balancing legacy lines locks in the old distribution and still gives the new line no quota.
Incorrect — the new line's share stays tiny at any volume, and a handful of samples cannot move the metric.
Incorrect — by the time production monitoring alerts, users are already hurt, and evaluation loses its pre-release gate role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上输入的分布随时间变化，偏离训练和测试时的分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distribution shift is when live input patterns drift away from the training and test distribution over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从数据中划出一部分完全不参与训练、只用于评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hold-out is a slice of data kept out of training and used only for evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长期固定不变的一组样本，用来检测模型退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A golden canary set is a fixed sample set kept stable over time to detect model degradation.

scenario: 团队想用线上日志离线估计新排序器的效果，于是用 importance weighting 给每条历史曝光按新旧策略的概率比重新加权。
scenario_en: To estimate a new ranker offline from production logs, the team reweights each logged impression by the ratio of new-policy to logging-policy probability.
q: 这种反事实估计的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of this counterfactual estimate?
why: 新策略与日志策略差异越大，少数样本的权重越极端，估计量方差爆炸——同一批日志换个随机切片结论就翻转；只能靠截断权重或补探索流量缓解。
why_en: The more the new policy diverges from the logging policy, the more extreme a few sample weights become, so variance explodes and the same logs can flip the conclusion.
options: 少数样本权重极端，估计方差很高，结论不稳定
需要把线上流量的百分之十长期划给新排序器，实验成本与直接做 A/B 完全一样
只能用于分类任务，排序问题里没有办法为每条曝光定义倾向性得分
会引入时间泄漏，因为重加权用到了发生在曝光之后的未来点击信息
options_en: A few samples get extreme weights, so the estimate has high variance and is unstable.
It needs ten percent of live traffic long-term, costing exactly as much as running a real A/B test.
It only works for classification, since ranking impressions have no definable propensity score.
It leaks time, because the reweighting uses click information that happened after the impression.
optionExplanations: 对；权重是概率比，新旧策略分歧大时个别样本能主导整个估计值。
错；反事实估计的卖点恰恰是复用已有日志，不需要新开线上流量。
错；排序里可以用日志策略展示该项的概率作为倾向性得分。
错；重加权只用曝光当时的策略概率，不涉及曝光之后发生的信息。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the weights are probability ratios, so when policies diverge a few samples can dominate the whole estimate.
Incorrect — the whole point of counterfactual estimation is reusing existing logs without new live traffic.
Incorrect — in ranking you can use the logging policy's display probability as the propensity score.
Incorrect — reweighting uses only the policy probability at impression time, not anything that happened later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用旧策略产生的日志估计如果换成新策略会怎样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Counterfactual evaluation uses logs from an old policy to estimate what a new policy would have done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按新旧策略选中同一条样本的概率之比给样本重新加权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Importance weighting rescales each logged sample by the ratio of new-policy to logging-policy probability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志策略当时展示该条目的概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A propensity score is the probability that the logging policy displayed that item at the time.

scenario: 新排序器离线指标很好，但它同时改动了候选生成，团队不敢直接把它的顺序推给真实用户。
scenario_en: A new ranker looks great offline but also changed candidate generation, and the team is not ready to serve its order to real users.
q: 上线前该先做哪种线上验证？
q_en: Which online validation should come first?
why: shadow-rank 让新模型重排但仍服务基线顺序，比较那些位次会变的物品上的点击，既拿到线上信号又零用户风险；代价是拿不到真实曝光后的行为。
why_en: Shadow-rank lets the new model reorder while the baseline order is still served, comparing clicks on items whose position would change — real online signal at zero user risk.
tradeoff: shadow-rank（零用户风险但拿不到真实曝光反馈）vs 直接 A/B（信号完整但坏模型会伤用户）
options: 跳过线上验证，直接把离线 NDCG 更高的模型全量替换掉现有的线上排序器
shadow-rank：模型重排但仍服务基线顺序，比较位次变化项的点击
把新旧模型的分数取平均后服务，用混合结果观察整体指标有没有下降
先只对内部员工开放新排序，等他们的主观反馈良好之后再考虑对外发布
options_en: Skip online validation and fully replace the live ranker with whichever model has higher offline NDCG.
Shadow-rank: the model reorders but the baseline order is still served, comparing clicks on items whose position changes.
Serve the average of both models' scores and watch whether the blended metrics drop.
Expose the new ranker to internal employees only and ship once their subjective feedback is good.
whenOtherWins: 如果改动很小且已有 shadow 结果，直接进 A/B 或 interleaving 更快拿到有统计功效的结论。
optionExplanations: 错；离线指标只是线上效用的近似，全量替换等于把风险直接压到用户身上。
对；用户看到的仍是基线顺序，却能收集到新模型判断有差异处的真实点击。
错；分数平均出来的是第三个模型，测不出新模型单独的效果。
错；员工不是目标用户分布，样本量和行为都无法代表线上流量。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — offline metrics only approximate online utility, so a full swap puts the risk straight onto users.
Correct — users still see the baseline order while you collect real clicks exactly where the new model disagrees.
Incorrect — averaging scores creates a third model and measures neither one on its own.
Incorrect — employees are not the target user distribution, so neither their volume nor behavior represents live traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新模型在线上打分排序但不对用户生效，只记录与基线的差异。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shadow-rank means the new model scores and ranks live but never affects users, only logging where it differs from the baseline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个排序器的结果混成一个列表给同一用户，形成成对比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving mixes two rankers' results into one list for the same user, turning the comparison into a paired test.

scenario: 电商搜索移动端首屏只显示 10 条结果，用户要滑动才能看到第 11 条以后；团队要选一个离线主排序指标。
scenario_en: Mobile product search shows 10 results above the fold, and users must scroll to reach the eleventh; the team must pick a primary offline ranking metric.
q: 离线排序指标的截断位 k 该由什么决定？
q_en: What should decide the cutoff k for the offline ranking metric?
why: 截断位 k 是产品参数而不是调参结果：首屏 10 条就优化 NDCG@10，指标才和用户实际看到的范围对齐；改版首屏条数时这个指标必须跟着改。
why_en: The cutoff k is a product parameter, not a tuning knob — ten results above the fold means optimize NDCG at 10 so the metric matches what users actually see.
tradeoff: k 对齐首屏（贴合用户实际所见）vs k 取更大值（数值更平滑但奖励了用户看不到的位置）
options: 产品界面首屏展示的结果条数，本例即 NDCG@10
让离线分数看起来最高的那个 k 值，通常取更大的 k 会让曲线更平滑好看
候选生成阶段召回回来的候选总数，一般是几百到上千条这个量级
训练集里每个 query 平均拥有的相关性标注条数，标了几条就取 k 等于几
options_en: The number of results the product UI shows above the fold, here NDCG at 10.
Whichever k makes the offline score look best, usually a larger k for a smoother curve.
The total number of candidates returned by candidate generation, typically hundreds to thousands.
The average number of graded relevance labels per query in the training set.
whenOtherWins: 如果界面是无限滚动、用户普遍会翻很深，就该取更大的 k 或改用不截断的 MAP。
optionExplanations: 对；用户看不到第 11 条，把它算进指标就是在优化没人看的位置。
错；按分数好看选 k 是自欺，指标会奖励用户根本触达不到的排名。
错；候选池大小是召回阶段的工程参数，和用户可见范围无关。
错；标注条数是数据集属性，改标注预算不该改变产品的成功定义。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — users never see the eleventh result, so counting it means optimizing positions nobody looks at.
Incorrect — picking k to flatter the score rewards ranks users cannot reach.
Incorrect — candidate pool size is a retrieval engineering parameter, unrelated to what users can see.
Incorrect — label count is a dataset property; changing the annotation budget should not redefine product success.

termDefinitions.fullName: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at k
termDefinitions.meaning: 只统计前 k 条结果、按位置折损相关性的归一化排序指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG at k scores only the top k results, discounting relevance by position and normalizing against the ideal order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均准确率均值：在每个相关结果处算 precision 再平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAP averages precision computed at each relevant result across queries.

scenario: 市场平台的推荐 NDCG 很高，但新入驻卖家几周都拿不到曝光，长尾商品几乎从不出现在任何推荐位上。
scenario_en: A marketplace recommender has strong NDCG, yet newly onboarded sellers get no impressions for weeks and long-tail items almost never appear.
q: 该补哪个产品指标来暴露这个问题？
q_en: Which product metric surfaces this problem?
why: 排序指标只衡量展示出的那几条排得对不对，完全看不见从没被展示过的目录部分；Coverage 统计时间窗内被展示过的目录比例，代价是提升它通常要牺牲短期 CTR。
why_en: Ranking metrics only judge the items that were shown and are blind to the catalog that was never surfaced; coverage measures the share of the catalog shown in a window.
tradeoff: 只优化排序质量（短期 CTR 高但长尾饿死）vs 纳入 Coverage（供给侧健康但短期指标下滑）
options: Coverage：时间窗内被展示过的目录比例
MRR：所有会话中第一个相关结果出现位置的平均倒数值有多高
响应延迟：从用户打开首页到推荐结果完成渲染之间的耗时
Recall@K：有多少比例的会话在前 K 条里至少命中了一个相关物品
options_en: Coverage: the share of the catalog surfaced within a time window.
MRR: the average reciprocal position of the first relevant result across all sessions.
Response latency: how long from opening the home page to recommendations rendering.
Recall at K: the share of sessions with at least one relevant item in the top K.
whenOtherWins: 如果目录很小且供给充足（例如只有几十部影片），Coverage 天然接近 100%，盯它没有信息量。
optionExplanations: 对；它直接统计目录被触达的广度，新卖家零曝光会立刻反映成低覆盖。
错；MRR 只看已展示结果里第一个相关项的位置，对没展示的商品无感。
错；延迟衡量渲染速度，和哪些商品被选中展示是两回事。
错；Recall@K 统计会话是否被满足，而会话可能全靠同一批热门品满足。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it measures how broadly the catalog is reached, so zero impressions for new sellers show up immediately as low coverage.
Incorrect — MRR only looks at the first relevant item among shown results and is blind to items never surfaced.
Incorrect — latency measures rendering speed, not which items get chosen for display.
Incorrect — recall at K asks whether sessions were satisfied, and they can be satisfied entirely by the same popular items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段时间窗口内被推荐展示过的目录条目比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coverage is the proportion of catalog items surfaced by recommendations over a time window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新卖家或新物品缺少交互数据，模型难以给它打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when a new seller or item has no interaction history for the model to score on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示出去的结果中被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR is click-through rate, the share of shown results that get clicked.

scenario: 短视频推荐把人均 dwell time 当作唯一北极星，模型上线后停留时长涨了 30%，三个月后次月留存却在持续下滑。
scenario_en: A short-video recommender uses dwell time as its single north star; dwell rose 30 percent after launch, but month-two retention has been sliding for three months.
q: 只优化 dwell time 会怎样反噬？
q_en: How does optimizing dwell time alone backfire?
why: 模型会学会制造 doom-scrolling：停留时长上去了但用户事后并不满意，短期指标吃掉长期留存；所以 dwell time 必须和留存这类长周期指标成对读。
why_en: The model learns to manufacture doom-scrolling — dwell goes up while satisfaction does not, so a short-term metric cannibalizes long-term retention.
options: 模型学会制造 doom-scrolling，停留变长但满意度和留存下滑
模型会偏向推荐时长更短的视频，因为短视频的完播率天然比长视频高得多
dwell time 无法按人群切片统计，所以任何分群上的回归都会被总体平均彻底掩盖
停留时长上升会直接推高推理成本，服务器扩容压力最终反噬到用户端的延迟
options_en: The model learns to manufacture doom-scrolling: dwell grows while satisfaction and retention fall.
The model favors shorter videos, since short clips naturally have far higher completion rates.
Dwell time cannot be sliced by audience, so any segment-level regression is hidden by the overall average.
Longer dwell drives up inference cost, and the scaling pressure eventually shows up as user-facing latency.
optionExplanations: 对；停留时长不区分看得投入和停不下来，模型只会挑更容易的那条路走。
错；优化停留时长的方向是拉长会话，不天然偏向更短的单条视频。
错；dwell time 完全可以按人群切片，切片不是这里的失败原因。
错；成本上升是运维问题，解释不了次月留存这个满意度信号在掉。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — dwell does not distinguish engaged watching from compulsive scrolling, and the model optimizes whichever is easier.
Incorrect — optimizing dwell pushes toward longer sessions, not inherently shorter individual clips.
Incorrect — dwell time can be sliced by audience segment, so slicing is not the failure here.
Incorrect — rising cost is an operations issue and does not explain a drop in month-two retention, a satisfaction signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在内容或页面上停留的时间长度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is how long a user stays on a piece of content or a page.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户停不下来地持续下滑浏览，事后满意度反而更低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doom-scrolling is compulsive continuous scrolling that leaves users less satisfied afterwards.

termDefinitions.term: north star metric / 北极星指标
termDefinitions.meaning: 团队长期对齐优化的那个唯一核心业务指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A north star metric is the single core business number a team aligns its optimization around.

scenario: 同一套推荐引擎要同时服务流媒体订阅站和零售商城；订阅站靠续费赚钱，商城按成交额抽佣且退货率高达两成。
scenario_en: One recommender engine serves both a subscription streaming site, which earns on renewals, and a retail marketplace, which takes a cut of sales with a 20 percent return rate.
q: 两边的北极星指标该分别选什么？
q_en: What should the north star metric be on each side?
why: 北极星要跟着钱走：订阅站的收入来自续费，completion rate 最能预测它；商城收入按成交抽佣，两成退货意味着必须扣掉退货后再算 GMV。
why_en: The north star follows the money — renewals make completion rate the right proxy for streaming, while commission on sales makes GMV net of returns the right one for retail.
tradeoff: completion rate（预测续费但对交易类业务无意义）vs 净退货后 GMV（贴合抽佣但对订阅制无意义）
options: 两边都用点击率，因为点击是所有推荐系统最通用也最容易采集的统一信号
流媒体看 completion rate，零售看净退货后的 GMV
两边都用总曝光量，曝光越多说明推荐引擎的服务吞吐和规模能力越强
流媒体看净退货后的 GMV，零售看 completion rate，交叉借鉴对方行业指标
options_en: Use click-through rate on both, since clicks are the most universal and easiest signal to collect.
Streaming tracks completion rate; retail tracks GMV net of returns.
Use total impressions on both, since more impressions show greater serving throughput.
Streaming tracks GMV net of returns and retail tracks completion rate, borrowing across industries.
whenOtherWins: 如果流媒体靠广告而不是订阅赚钱，观看时长和广告曝光就比 completion rate 更贴近收入。
optionExplanations: 错；点击既不代表看完一集，也不代表成交后没被退货，离两边的收入都很远。
对；各自选最接近收入的下游动作：看完一集预示续费，净成交额才是抽佣基数。
错；曝光量是系统吞吐指标，推得越多不代表用户价值或收入越高。
错；订阅制没有成交额可算，交易平台也没有看完这个动作。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — a click neither means an episode was finished nor that a purchase survived returns, so it is far from either revenue line.
Correct — each picks the downstream action closest to revenue: finishing an episode predicts renewal, and net sales is the commission base.
Incorrect — impressions measure system throughput; serving more does not mean more user value or revenue.
Incorrect — a subscription business has no sales total, and a marketplace has no completion action.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商品交易总额：平台上成交商品的总金额。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GMV is gross merchandise value, the total money value of goods transacted on the platform.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开始观看的内容中被看完的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Completion rate is the share of started content that viewers finish.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示结果中被点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR is click-through rate, the share of shown results that get clicked.

scenario: 站内搜索里绝大多数 query 是一次性的长尾词，标注预算只够覆盖头部几千个 query。
scenario_en: In site search most queries are one-off long-tail terms, and the labeling budget only covers a few thousand head queries.
q: 长尾 query 的相关性怎么评估？
q_en: How do you evaluate relevance on long-tail queries?
why: 长尾 query 数量上不封顶，逐条人工标注在预算上不可能；用大模型做零样本相关性判定替代显式标注，代价是要定期用人工标注抽查校准它。
why_en: Long-tail queries are effectively unbounded, so per-query human labels are unaffordable; use a large model for zero-shot relevance judgments and calibrate it with human spot checks.
tradeoff: 人工标注（高精度但只覆盖头部）vs 大模型零样本判定（可覆盖长尾但需持续校准）
options: 只评估头部几千个 query，长尾部分默认与头部表现一致，不再单独衡量
用大模型做零样本相关性判定替代显式标注
把标注预算从头部转移到长尾，优先标注那些一年只出现过一次的稀有 query
把长尾 query 全部改写成最接近的头部 query 再评估，用改写后的分数代表长尾
options_en: Evaluate only the few thousand head queries and assume the tail performs the same.
Use a large language model for zero-shot relevance judgments instead of explicit labels.
Move the labeling budget from head to tail, prioritizing queries seen once a year.
Rewrite every tail query to its nearest head query and report the rewritten score.
whenOtherWins: 如果领域高度专业（如医疗、法律），模型判定不可信，仍要靠专家标注加 query 聚类共享判定。
optionExplanations: 错；长尾正是模型最弱的地方，用头部表现外推等于系统性高估质量。
对；零样本判定能低成本覆盖任意 query，再用人工抽查维持它的可信度。
错；一次性 query 标了也不会再出现，预算换不来可复用的评估资产。
错；改写会把长尾的真实意图抹平，测到的还是头部而不是长尾表现。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — the tail is where the model is weakest, so extrapolating from head performance systematically overstates quality.
Correct — zero-shot judgment covers arbitrary queries cheaply, with human spot-checks keeping it trustworthy.
Incorrect — a once-a-year query never recurs, so the budget buys no reusable evaluation asset.
Incorrect — rewriting erases the tail query's real intent, so you end up measuring head performance again.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出现频次极低但种类极多的那部分查询或内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The long tail is the huge variety of queries or items that each occur very rarely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不给任务专门的训练样本，直接让模型按指令做判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zero-shot means asking the model to judge from instructions alone, with no task-specific training examples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相似查询归到一组，让它们共享相关性标注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query clustering groups similar queries so they can share relevance judgments.

scenario: 内容审核模型分 12 个违规类别，报表只给一个整体 precision 0.94，运营却反馈某个小类几乎全靠人工兜底。
scenario_en: A moderation model covers 12 violation classes and reports a single overall precision of 0.94, yet operations says one small class is handled almost entirely by humans.
q: 只报总体指标会漏掉什么？
q_en: What does reporting only the overall metric miss?
why: 多分类系统必须报 per-class 性能：占比小的类别在总体平均里权重极低，可以整类崩掉而总分纹丝不动，运营的人工兜底量成了它唯一的外部信号。
why_en: Multi-class systems need per-class performance — a small class can fail completely while the overall average barely moves, leaving manual workload as its only visible signal.
options: 小类别整类崩掉也不会拉动总分，per-class 指标才能暴露
总体指标算不出 recall 只能算 precision，所以漏放情况天然无法被任何报表观察到
12 个类别之间存在标签重叠，任何总体指标在多标签设定下都不具备数学意义
总体指标只在测试集上成立，线上流量分布不同因此所有离线数字都不该被采信
options_en: A small class can fail entirely without moving the overall number; only per-class metrics expose it.
Overall metrics cannot produce recall, only precision, so misses are inherently unobservable in any report.
The 12 classes overlap, so no aggregate metric is mathematically meaningful in a multi-label setting.
Overall metrics hold only on the test set, so every offline number should be distrusted outright.
optionExplanations: 对；总体平均按样本量加权，占 1% 的类别几乎不影响那个 0.94。
错；总体 recall 完全可以计算，问题在于它同样被大类主导。
错；类别重叠是标签设计问题，与只报总体这个报表口径无关。
错；离线数字仍有价值，问题是粒度太粗而不是离线评估本身不可信。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the overall average is weighted by volume, so a class holding one percent of samples barely touches that 0.94.
Incorrect — overall recall is perfectly computable; the issue is that it too is dominated by large classes.
Incorrect — overlapping labels is a label-design question, unrelated to reporting only an aggregate.
Incorrect — offline numbers still have value; the problem is granularity, not offline evaluation itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对每个类别单独统计 precision、recall，而不是只看总体平均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-class performance reports precision and recall separately for each class instead of one overall average.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输出要从三个以上互斥类别中选一个的分类任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-class classification picks one label from three or more mutually exclusive classes.

scenario: 欺诈检测里正例不到 1%，模型只在已知作案模式上表现好；一种全新手法出现时，它既不报警也几乎不会被随机抽样抽到。
scenario_en: In fraud detection positives are under 1 percent and the model only handles known patterns; a brand-new scheme neither triggers alerts nor gets caught by random sampling.
q: 该建一条什么样的循环来发现新型少数类？
q_en: What kind of loop should you build to discover new minority-class cases?
why: 新手法在训练数据里没有标签、模型分数天然偏低，随机抽样也几乎抽不到；靠主动学习优先送审不确定或新颖的样本再回灌训练集，代价是持续占用人工审核预算。
why_en: A new scheme has no labels and scores low by construction, and random sampling almost never hits it; active learning routes uncertain or novel cases to review and feeds findings back into training.
tradeoff: 随机抽样送审（无偏但对 1% 正例效率极低）vs 主动学习按不确定性送审（发现率高但引入采样偏差）
options: 主动学习：优先把不确定或新颖的样本送人工审核，结果回灌训练集
把模型的报警阈值整体调低，让更多交易被判为欺诈从而提高整体召回覆盖面
扩大随机抽样的规模，每天多抽十倍交易送人工复核以提高命中新手法的概率
在训练时对已知欺诈样本做过采样，让模型对现有欺诈模式学得更充分更敏感
options_en: Active learning: route uncertain or novel samples to human review and feed the results back into training.
Lower the alert threshold across the board so more transactions get flagged and overall recall rises.
Scale up random sampling, sending ten times more transactions to review each day to raise the odds of hitting new schemes.
Oversample known fraud during training so the model learns existing fraud patterns more sharply.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是无偏估计欺诈的真实发生率（prevalence），就必须用随机抽样而不是主动学习。
optionExplanations: 对；按不确定性和新颖度选样，把有限审核预算花在模型最可能出错的地方。
错；降阈值放大的是已知模式的边缘案例，新手法分数低照样被挡在阈值之下。
错；正例不到 1%，抽十倍只是把极低命中率线性放大，成本先撑不住。
错；过采样只会让模型对已知模式更自信，对没见过的手法毫无帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — selecting by uncertainty and novelty spends the limited review budget where the model is most likely wrong.
Incorrect — a lower threshold surfaces edge cases of known patterns, while a new scheme still scores below it.
Incorrect — with under one percent positives, ten times the sampling only scales a tiny hit rate linearly and the cost breaks first.
Incorrect — oversampling only makes the model more confident on known patterns and does nothing for unseen ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按标了最有信息量的原则挑样本送标注，而不是随机挑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Active learning picks the most informative samples to label instead of sampling randomly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 正负样本比例极度悬殊，正例只占很小一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Class imbalance is when positives make up only a tiny fraction of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据中真实正例所占的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prevalence is the true share of positive cases in production data.
